config.title: Real-Time Board

intro.title: Real-Time Board
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a real-time collaborative board application where multiple users can add, move, and edit sticky notes simultaneously. You'll learn how to implement WebSocket communication to enable instant data synchronization between different browser sessions, ensuring all users see changes as they happen. The project uses Angular's reactive programming with RxJS observables to handle real-time data streams, component communication through services, and dynamic DOM manipulation for drag-and-drop interactions. You'll work with Angular services to manage WebSocket connections, implement event handling for user interactions, and use Angular's change detection to update the UI automatically when data changes. By the end, you'll understand how to create responsive, multi-user applications that update in real-time without page refreshes.
intro.usecase: Real-time boards are essential for collaborative applications like project management tools (Trello, Asana), team communication platforms (Slack channels), and live dashboards (analytics, monitoring systems). Developers implement these patterns when building features like live comment sections, collaborative document editing, stock price displays, or multiplayer game boards where multiple users need to see updates instantly. Modern web applications rely on real-time data synchronization to keep users engaged and informed, making this a critical skill for building responsive, interactive user experiences that feel dynamic and connected.

objectives: Initialize WebSocket connections to enable real-time data communication
Implement event listeners to capture and handle board interaction events
Configure Angular services to manage real-time state synchronization
Construct dynamic board components that update based on incoming data streams
Apply reactive programming patterns to bind live data to board elements
Integrate real-time updates with Angular's change detection cycle
Manipulate board state to reflect concurrent user interactions across sessions

steps.instruction: Import Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from @angular/core, and import a WebSocketService from a websocket service file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the required Angular lifecycle interfaces and the Component decorator, plus create an import for the WebSocket service that will handle real-time communication.

successCriteria: Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy are imported from @angular/core, and WebSocketService is imported from a service file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

// Create the RealTimeBoardComponent here

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Initialize component properties and board state
steps.instruction: Add three properties to the RealTimeBoardComponent class: boardData as an empty array, isConnected as false, and currentUser as null.
steps.hint: In Angular components, class properties are declared directly inside the class body without keywords like 'let' or 'const'. Initialize each property with its starting value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have three properties initialized to track the board state, connection status, and current user information.
successCriteria: The component has boardData initialized as an empty array, isConnected initialized as false, and currentUser initialized as null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have all three properties: boardData (empty array), isConnected (false), and currentUser (null).
steps.feedbackWrong: add three class properties inside the component: boardData as an empty array, isConnected as false, and currentUser as null.

steps.instruction: Add a constructor to the RealTimeBoardComponent that injects the WebSocketService using Angular dependency injection.
steps.hint: Use the constructor keyword and inject the service by declaring it as a parameter with private access modifier.

// Similar: injecting a service in Angular
constructor(private userService: UserService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a constructor that injects the WebSocketService, making it available for real-time communication throughout the component.
successCriteria: Constructor is added to RealTimeBoardComponent with WebSocketService injected as a private parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using the private access modifier and the correct service name (WebSocketService).
steps.feedbackWrong: add a constructor that takes WebSocketService as a parameter with the private keyword for dependency injection.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an ngOnInit method that establishes a WebSocket connection and subscribes to board updates when the component initializes
successCriteria: ngOnInit method is implemented and connects to WebSocket service with subscription to board updates
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ngOnInit method both connects to the WebSocket and subscribes to incoming board updates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should establish a WebSocket connection and set up subscription to board updates. Try implementing the lifecycle method with these actions.

steps.hint: Create a method that accepts incoming board data and assigns it to the component's board property to reflect real-time changes.
steps.expectedOutcome: A method named 'onBoardUpdate' is added to handle incoming board data and update the component's board state
successCriteria: The onBoardUpdate method is defined with a data parameter and updates the board property

steps.title: Wire form submission to creation handler
steps.instruction: Wrap the input and button in a form element and add an ngSubmit event binding to call the createItem method when the form is submitted.
steps.hint: Use Angular's (ngSubmit) directive on the form element to handle form submission. This will call your createItem method when the user presses Enter or clicks the button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Form with ngSubmit event binding
<form (ngSubmit)="saveData()">
  <input type="text" [(ngModel)]="data">
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The input and button are wrapped in a form element with an (ngSubmit) event binding that calls the createItem method, enabling form submission via Enter key or button click.
successCriteria: A form element wraps the input and button with (ngSubmit)="createItem()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to wrap both the input and button in a form element and add the (ngSubmit) event binding to call createItem.
steps.feedbackWrong: wrap the input and button in a form element and add (ngSubmit)="createItem()" to handle form submission.

steps.title: Implement ngOnDestroy for cleanup
steps.instruction: Add an ngOnDestroy method to the RealTimeBoardComponent that closes the WebSocket connection when the component is destroyed
steps.hint: Use ngOnDestroy lifecycle hook to call this.webSocketService.close() for proper cleanup and preventing memory leaks
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an ngOnDestroy method that properly closes the WebSocket connection when the component is destroyed
successCriteria: ngOnDestroy method is implemented and calls webSocketService.close() for cleanup
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ngOnDestroy method calls this.webSocketService.close() to properly clean up the WebSocket connection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnDestroy method should close the WebSocket connection using this.webSocketService.close() to prevent memory leaks when the component is destroyed.
